title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 3

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the comparison lesson begin?
tasks.audioText: The manufacturing tutor will compare turning, milling and drilling in a theory lesson on Tuesday at ten thirty. Students should bring the process chart from the previous class. The tutor will focus on the type of movement and the feature produced by each process. Practical demonstrations will be scheduled separately after the workshop equipment has been checked.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which machining reference material is needed for the session?
tasks.audioText: The manufacturing tutor will compare turning, milling and drilling in a theory lesson on Tuesday at ten thirty. Students should bring the process chart from the previous class. The tutor will focus on the type of movement and the feature produced by each process. Practical demonstrations will be scheduled separately after the workshop equipment has been checked.
options: The component drawing from the previous class
The process chart from the previous class
The machine manual from the previous class
The safety checklist from the previous class

tasks.prompt: Turning is commonly used to produce cylindrical surfaces, while milling can create flat surfaces, slots and more complex profiles. Drilling produces a round hole using a rotating drill. The correct process depends on the component drawing, material and required geometry. A process plan usually lists the main stages and the equipment category, but detailed settings must be taken from approved process documentation. Reading 1. Which operation is commonly used to produce a cylindrical surface?
What information helps determine the correct process?
options: The machine availability, operator shift and delivery date
The component colour, storage location and supplier
The cutting-tool brand, lubricant and batch number
The drawing, material and required geometry

tasks.prompt: Slots and flat surfaces ___ by milling in many applications.
Choose TWO machining operations paired with their typical results.
The machining operation commonly used to produce a round hole is ___.
A drawing shows a cylindrical outside surface. Which question is most useful?
options: Would turning be an appropriate process for this geometry?

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of machining operations in a logical order.
Write 80–100 words comparing turning, milling and drilling. Describe the typical result of each operation and explain why the drawing matters.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: turning, milling and drilling are all described with their typical results (0–2); the response explains why the drawing defines required geometry/features and provides the reference for the work (0–2); comparisons are logically organised with understandable grammar (0–2); machining/drawing vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
